extra.message: User input from req.query.red is passed directly to eval() in the /cwe95/rgbToHex route handler. This is eval injection: an attacker can supply arbitrary JavaScript (e.g. require('child_process').exec(...)) and achieve remote code execution. The value should be parsed with parseInt(req.query.red, 10) instead.

User input from req.query.green is passed directly to eval() in the /cwe95/rgbToHex route handler. This is eval injection: an attacker can supply arbitrary JavaScript and achieve remote code execution. The value should be parsed with parseInt(req.query.green, 10) instead.

User input from req.query.blue is passed directly to eval() in the /cwe95/rgbToHex route handler. This is eval injection: an attacker can supply arbitrary JavaScript and achieve remote code execution. The value should be parsed with parseInt(req.query.blue, 10) instead.

The /cwe73/read route passes the user-controlled query parameter req.query.foo directly to fse.readJsonSync() as a file path without any validation or allowlisting. An attacker can supply an arbitrary path (e.g. ../../ etc/passwd or any file reachable on the server) and have the server read and return its contents, giving an arbitrary file read (external control of file name or path / path traversal).

cwe: CWE-73: External Control of File Name or Path
CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message:
The /cwe79/echo route concatenates the user-controlled query parameter req.query.text directly into an HTML string ('

You sent this: ' + req.query.text + '

') that is returned via res.send() without HTML escaping, enabling reflected cross-site scripting, e.g. /cwe79/echo?text=.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: The /cwe113/split route sets an HTTP response header whose name (req.query.key) and value (req.query.value) are both taken directly from user input via res.append() without neutralizing CRLF sequences. An attacker can inject CR/LF characters to split the HTTP response and inject arbitrary headers (HTTP response splitting / header injection).

cwe: CWE-113: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences in HTTP Headers ('HTTP Response Splitting')

extra.message: The /cwe201/exposure route reflects the raw user-supplied query parameter req.query.text back in the response via res.send() without any filtering. Sensitive data supplied by the client is echoed unmodified (information exposure through sent data), and because it is carried in the URL it is also exposed in server/proxy logs and browser history.

cwe: CWE-201: Information Exposure Through Sent Data

extra.message: The /cwe601/redirect route builds the redirect target by concatenating the user-controlled query parameter req.query.text into the URL passed to res.redirect() without validation or URL-encoding. Untrusted input is embedded in the redirect Location header, allowing an attacker to manipulate the redirect target (open redirect pattern) and to inject unencoded data into an HTTP header.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: The /cwe502/serialize route passes the user-controlled query parameter req.query.foo to serialize.unserialize() from the node-serialize (0.0.4) library, which deserializes untrusted data and supports executable function payloads via the _$$ND_FUNC$$_ prefix. An attacker can achieve remote code execution, e.g. ?foo={"rce":"_$$ND_FUNC$$_function (){require('child_process').exec('...')}()"}.

The /cwe78/childprocess route passes the user-controlled query parameter req.query.foo directly to cprocess.exec(), which executes it through the system shell. This allows arbitrary OS command execution on the server (command injection), e.g. ?foo=cat%20%2Fetc%2Fpasswd.

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
